I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 30 years, and I know every corner of my 50 mu. My family has seven mouths to feed, and with some of them working off-farm, I have a bit of cash coming in, but I am short on labor during busy seasons. That means I cannot afford to waste time or money on things that do not pay back.

For wheat, I will plant the full 50 mu with an improved variety. I have learned that hybrid seeds for wheat are not worth the extra cost here, but a good improved variety like the ones I have used in recent years gives me steady yields. I will rotary till before planting to get a fine seedbed. I will put down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu — split between basal and top-dressing at the jointing stage — because too much nitrogen just makes the wheat lodge and wastes money. I will add some phosphorus and potassium too, around 6 and 5 kg per mu, since the soil here needs it after years of maize-wheat rotation. Water is from my well, so I pay for the electricity. I will irrigate three times: once in late autumn or early winter to protect the seedlings from cold, once at jointing when the wheat starts growing fast in spring, and once at heading or grain filling. I will spray pesticides twice — once in spring for aphids and diseases, and once around heading if needed. I expect about 520 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For maize, timing is everything because I have to plant right after wheat harvest in early June before the soil dries out. I will use hybrid seed — Zhengdan or something similar — because hybrid maize really does outperform here. I will use no-tillage and plant directly into the wheat stubble. This saves me fuel, time, and labor, which matters when my family is busy. I will apply about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 5 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. Maize needs water at the critical stages, so I will irrigate twice: once around the big flare stage when the tassels and silks are out, and once during grain filling. I will spray twice for weeds and corn borers. With good summer rainfall and two irrigations, I should get around 600 kg per mu.

I do not take big risks anymore. I stick with what works, keep input costs reasonable, and make sure I have enough labor or hired help for harvest.
